rv.q: ‘Scene Partners,’ by John J. Caswell Jr., with the transcendent Dianne Wiest as Meryl, is definitely more like whoa. Twee, snarky, meta, manic, maddening and yet eventually poignant, the play is a moving target, its tone as hard to pin down as its facts.

It takes an artist of the stature and extraordinary talent of Wiest to keep Caswell’s fragmented play from flying off in all directions as it veers from reality to fantasy and from flashback to the present.
Scene Partners may be negligible, but it is a welcome opportunity to savor the two-time Oscar-winning Ms. Wiest's tremendous talent onstage as Meryl Kowalski.
But the solid production can't completely compensate for the elusiveness of the script.
How disappointing, then, that the play prevents any of them from making a memorable impression.
But it's all kind of incoherent — narratively, structurally, tonally.
After 100 lethargic minutes of Scene Partners, it's unlikely you'll care one way or another.
Caswell has crafted a truly engaging, enervating piece of theater.
Scene Partners has less structure to hold on to, and a penchant for fast pivots, leaving its audience to tumble out of the theater off-balance.

In spite of the refined direction by Rachel Chavkin and the aforementioned excellent performances all around, it is this writer's opinion that without Dianne Wiest there would indeed be 'nothing there.'
